facts.fact: TechCabal reports that the South African Reserve Bank published a May 2026 draft framework for non-bank payment and e-money authorisation, with a final authorisation framework planned by end November 2026 per Governor Kganyago.

ZAF.note: Only fee levels are discussed; no conduct rules or complaints body.
Nothing on government payments to people.
Nothing on government technical staff or systems.

facts.fact: TechCabal reports that SARB's May 2026 draft framework would let approved non-banks issue e-money and accept merchant payments, with initial capital of R3 million for merchant acquirers and R5 million or R8 million for e-money issuers.

ZAF.note: Only an account-holder count for one product, no adult survey.

facts.fact: TechCabal reports that PayShap, a shared instant-payment service used by participating banks, is in service, and that SARB Governor Kganyago said on 20 October 2026 it processed about 6% as many transactions as cards last year.

ZAF.note: Nothing on tax or fee payment.
